335ce78a38.q: How did Hunter Gimbel grow Gaber Group through partnership with other financial professionals like Howard Sharkman?
335ce78a38.a: Hunter Gimbel became strategic partners with Howard Sharkman through the Penn Mutual Star Study Group over the last four or five years. Although they work in completely different firms, they have worked together on numerous cases, providing value to clients across the continental US in private equity and banking, both for existing clients and referrals. This collaboration allowed Gimbel to deepen his bench without necessarily adding someone internally to the firm.
335ce78a38.e: The Partnership Advantage: How Top Financial Professionals Grow and Win More Business
335ce78a38.rq: If you want to provide the best value and work with really successful individuals and families, having two advisors or maybe even three advisors working with a really successful family along with their other advisors—it takes a village to get things done the right way.

5037857a3c.q: How does Gaber Group prepare clients before they meet with trust and estate attorneys to reduce legal fees?
5037857a3c.a: Gaber Group does internal design work and maps everything out so that by the time a client meets with a trust and estate lawyer, their entire estate diagram is filled out and completed. This makes the attorney's job easier and saves clients probably 20% to 30% of the estate planning fee, and cuts down the time from wanting to update estate planning to execution from six to twelve months to three to four months for most clients.

aaf3f79dd7.q: What advice does Hunter Gimbel give financial professionals starting to build partnerships for the first time?
aaf3f79dd7.a: Gimbel recommends ensuring you have the same culture, beliefs, and are comfortable with the advisor. It is also helpful if they work inside the markets or with the types of clients you serve. He suggests reaching out to Penn Mutual's advanced planning team or your managing director to identify the right partner or partners, and notes that not all joint work partnerships will work—it may take trying different people and organizations to find the right fit.
